To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) augmenting a credit risk model with information about the interfirm financial transaction network improves the model's prediction performance; (2) the effect of interfirm transaction network on credit risk is stronger for companies with higher credit risk; (3) the interfirm transaction network effect is stronger for companies that are more exposed to the financial system and for those that are more financially dependent on other companies.
the inclusion of information on interfirm transactions in a credit risk model significantly increases its predictive power.

the inclusion of information on interfirm financial transactions improves the predictive performance of credit risk models for small and medium enterprises, and that the improvement in the predictive performance is significant and economically meaningful.

the effect of interfirm transactions on the creditworthiness of small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and the potential for using this information in the development of a new credit scoring system.
the credit risk of SMEs, which is an important topic in the current context of the Covid‐19 pandemic and the resulting financial distress.
the effect of interfirm links on the credit risk and performance of small and medium sized enterprises.
